blind_solve.my_reasoning: Randomised invitation with identical cumulative incidence (excludes overdiagnosis), identical cancer deaths, and an identical distribution of tumour grades and growth rates (excludes length-time), yet survival measured from the date of diagnosis is longer: the only thing that has changed is the moment the survival clock starts, which is lead-time bias.

The letter's sole benefit statement is an unanchored relative risk reduction with no denominator and no harms, so the revision that most improves the reader's ability to make an informed choice is to replace it with the absolute chance of benefit plus the commonest harm (false positives); sensitivity and specificity are excluded by the stated limited numeracy, and a bare detection count is uninterpretable without a denominator.

A screening programme must not be launched where confirmatory investigation is effectively unavailable (a single clinic with a fourteen-month wait) and there is no funded treatment pathway, because labelling asymptomatic people who then cannot be investigated or treated is itself the harm the criterion exists to prevent.

Attendance was voluntary with no allocation, attenders smoked less and exercised more at baseline, and their mortality is lower even from causes screening cannot affect (road traffic collisions), which is the signature of pre-existing between-group differences rather than any measurement artefact of screening.

findings: Internal coherence checked and holds. Equal cumulative incidence plus equal cancer deaths at a fixed twelve years from randomisation is fully compatible with 'mean survival measured from the date of diagnosis is four years longer in the invited group', because the survival origin (date of diagnosis) has moved while the date of death has not. This is the defining arithmetic of lead-time bias and the stem gets it right.

reasoning_demand PASS on a specific test: the item is NOT solvable by mapping the buzzword 'survival' to 'lead-time bias'. Length-time bias and overdiagnosis would ALSO lengthen survival measured from diagnosis without a mortality benefit, so the candidate must additionally use 'the cumulative number of people diagnosed with the cancer is the same in both groups' to exclude overdiagnosis and 'the same distribution of tumour grades and growth rates' to exclude length-time. Three of the four options survive the single salient cue; only the exclusion clauses separate them.

Every named bias mechanism is described accurately. Distractor B rationale: 'Slowly progressing variants stay in the pre-symptomatic screen-detectable stage longer than rapidly progressing ones, so intermittent screening detects a disproportionate number of them' is an accurate statement of length-time bias and matches CLM-R2-PHELO-LENGTH. Distractor D rationale: 'That mechanism requires more cases in the screened group' is the correct operational signature of overdiagnosis (excess cumulative incidence persisting after adequate follow-up).

numeric_correctness: the only numerals are 'twelve years', 'four years longer' and, in the D rationale, 'up to thirty per cent more cancers are diagnosed in the screened than in the unscreened group', which reproduces CLM-R2-PHELO-OVERDIAGNOSIS ('up to 30% more breast cancers') without inflation. No candidate-facing proportion rests on anything unverified.

Note (not scored as a failure): all three distractors are anchored by mention-then-exclusion rather than by a positively suggestive fact. Option A's anchor is 'Participants were randomly allocated to be invited or not invited, and the two groups were comparable at baseline', which is a refuting anchor; the pull toward A comes mainly from the generic 'a screened group looks better' habit. It is the weakest of the three distractors, but the randomisation clause is a fact the candidate must actively read and apply, so it remains a legitimate trap for a candidate who reaches for selection bias reflexively.

material_redundancy vs G2-PHELO-05: NOT redundant in the decision tested. This item's discriminator is that an unchanged mortality with a changed survival-from-diagnosis means the clock origin moved (an RCT, measurement-artefact decision); G2-PHELO-05's is that lower mortality from causes screening cannot affect means the groups differed before screening began (an observational, confounding decision). Neither key is reachable by the other item's reasoning. The overlap is presentational and is described in the G2-PHELO-05 entry.

one_best_answer FAIL. Option A is defensibly best and the item never decisively excludes it. The stem says 'The present letter states only that screening reduces the risk of dying from the disease by thirty per cent', and 'states only' means the letter also omits any statement that participation is voluntary. The declared objective is stated twice in the most autonomy-specific terms available: 'the objective of this revision is to protect the autonomy of the people invited, and that raising uptake is explicitly not the objective'. Voluntariness and freedom from implied compulsion is the core of autonomy; interpretability of a benefit figure is the core of informed choice. The lead-in asks for autonomy, not for numerical comprehension.

one_best_answer FAIL, second and stronger limb: the item's OWN admitted evidence supports option A and is never rebutted. CLM-R2-PHELO-REMINDERS states 'Sending patients letters or other reminders improves screening uptake, however if patients perceive the reminders as having more authority than they do they may abdicate their right to informed consent.' That claim is about precisely this artefact (an official programme invitation letter) and precisely this failure mode (abdication of the right to informed consent). A candidate who has read the same source and applies that claim selects A. Admitting a claim into the item that supports a distractor, while the key rests on different claims, leaves two evidence-backed answers.

one_best_answer FAIL, third limb: the rebuttal offered for A is an assertion of priority, not a discriminator. Distractor rationale A reads 'Voluntariness is a real component of informed choice and the programme's own criterion requires informed consent and protection of autonomy, so this edit serves the stated objective. The letter's actual defect is that its only statement of benefit is a relative figure with no denominator and no harms; telling a reader the choice is free does not make the information on which they choose interpretable.' The first sentence concedes the option serves the stated objective; the second simply nominates a different defect as 'the actual' one. Nothing in the stem ranks the two defects. Concrete fix: add one clause to the stem stating that the letter already says participation is voluntary and that declining will not affect other care. That single edit makes A a genuine but clearly redundant revision and leaves C uniquely best, with no other change required.

Potential secondary concern examined and CLEARED. The stem's numeracy clause is narrowly drawn: 'whose numeracy the programme's own testing found to be limited, so figures expressing test performance are not reliably interpreted by the readers'. It excludes D without self-defeating for C, because absolute risks and a false-positive frequency are not 'figures expressing test performance', and the health-literacy position that absolute risks and natural frequencies are interpretable where sensitivity and specificity are not is a real and defensible distinction, not an ad hoc carve-out. The wording is close to the line but the distinction is substantively correct, so cueing is PASS.

factual_correctness and numeric_correctness PASS. 'thirty per cent' as a relative risk reduction reproduces the example in CLM-R4-PHELO-ABSOLUTE ('reduce the risk of death from breast cancer by 30%'), and the key rationale's 'roughly ten per cent of women screened for the first time undergo further testing only to find the result was falsely positive' reproduces CLM-R4-PHELO-FALSEPOS ('About 10% of women who undergo breast cancer screening for the first time'). Both are correctly stated and correctly applied, and neither number appears in an option, so nothing candidate-facing depends on them.

Minor, not scored as a failure: the key rationale imports a breast-screening-specific false-positive rate into an item whose programme and disease are unspecified ('the disease'). The rationale keeps the original 'women' framing so it does not misstate the source, but the illustrative figure is not strictly transferable to the unnamed programme in the stem; it is rationale-facing only.

distractor_competitiveness PASS. Each distractor has a positive stem anchor: A is anchored by 'states only' (voluntariness is absent) and by the autonomy framing; B is anchored by 'It gives no absolute figures, no denominator' (a detection count reads as supplying a missing number); D is anchored by 'no description of the harms of screening' plus the numeracy clause, which a candidate may misread as an argument for supplying more precise test data. All four options are edits to the same letter and at the same grain of decision.
material_redundancy PASS: this is the only autonomy/communication item in the group; it shares no discriminator with G2-PHELO-01, -03 or -05.

distractor_competitiveness FAIL on option D, 'Commission an economic evaluation before deciding'. The stem states 'a completed economic evaluation shows it to be good value for money'. That is a direct verbal contradiction of the option, requiring no epidemiological or ethical reasoning to detect: the option asks for a thing the stem says in plain words has already been done and has already returned a favourable result. Contrast the other two distractors, whose exclusion demands actual inference (A requires knowing that evaluation is a launch condition rather than a substitute for capacity; B requires seeing that a smaller launch still feeds a single clinic with no treatment pathway). D is a giveaway option that reduces the item to a three-option question for any candidate who reads the stem, and the item's own text concedes this: distractor rationale D says 'It has already been done and shows the programme to be good value for money, so it is not the open question.' Note this is not COMPETITOR_WITHOUT_STEM_ANCHOR: the anchor exists ('a completed economic evaluation') but it is purely refuting, so the option is anchored without being tempting. Fix: remove the completed economic evaluation from the stem, so a candidate must weigh cost-effectiveness evidence against the capacity gap and D becomes a live wrong answer; or replace D with a competitor that a partially knowledgeable candidate would actually choose, e.g. launching while commissioning additional diagnostic capacity in parallel.

one_best_answer PASS. Option B is the only serious competitor and is correctly closed off. The shortfall is absolute, not proportional: 'there is no funded pathway to treatment for those confirmed', so a single-district pilot still screens people who, if positive, cannot be investigated within a reasonable time or treated at all. The rationale states this precisely: 'The authority has costed the capacity and has the money; what is missing is the staff and the clinic itself, so a smaller launch still screens people who cannot be investigated or treated.'

factual_correctness PASS. The ethics and the screening criteria are stated correctly and match the admitted evidence: CLM-R2-PHELO-FACILITIES ('If waiting lists are long or if facilities for follow up and treatment are not conveniently accessible, the screening program should be reconsidered'), CLM-R2-PHELO-ACCEPTED-TREATMENT ('There should be an accepted treatment for patients with recognized disease') and CLM-R4-PHELO-HARM-LABEL ('Harm occurs when asymptomatic people are labelled as possibly having a disease but further investigation cannot be carried out, and harm also occurs when they are diagnosed and no treatment offered'). Each is applied to the correct stem fact.

numeric_correctness and critical_fact_safety PASS. The only numerals are 'next month', 'one diagnostic clinic' and 'fourteen months'; none is a rate, proportion or interval requiring external verification, and the fourteen-month wait is used only qualitatively, as an instance of the 'waiting lists are long' criterion. No option contains a number.

Distractor A is correctly neutralised without being trivial: the stem's 'The programme has written goals and an evaluation plan' gives A a real positive anchor (CLM-R4-PHELO-EVALUATION is a genuine criterion the programme meets), and the rebuttal that 'Evaluation is a condition of launching rather than a substitute for the confirmatory and treatment capacity that is absent' is the correct distinction.

cueing PASS: the key is not the longest, most specific or most qualified option, and the stem does not lexically signal it. anchor_fidelity and plan_fidelity PASS: the item asks for a launch decision and turns exactly on the declared discriminator, 'an absolute absence of the confirmatory and treatment pathway, not cost, not logistics and not the cut-off'. The validated cut-off clause and the completed costing are correctly deployed as decoy-closing facts for the cut-off and cost routes.
material_redundancy PASS: no other item in the group tests a launch/defer decision or the availability-of-treatment criterion.

factual_correctness FAIL: the stem asserts a combination of results that is arithmetically impossible. It states (i) 'the attenders have lower mortality from the screened disease', (ii) 'The cumulative number of people diagnosed with the disease is the same in both groups', and (iii) 'survival measured from diagnosis does not differ between the groups'. Disease-specific mortality in a population equals cumulative incidence multiplied by case fatality over the follow-up period. If cumulative incidence is identical (ii) and survival measured from diagnosis is identical (iii), then case fatality over the ten years is identical and disease-specific mortality must be EQUAL in the two groups, contradicting (i). Equivalently: lower disease mortality with the same number of people diagnosed necessarily means fewer of those diagnosed died, which is by definition better survival from diagnosis. There is no configuration of the three stipulations that can co-exist.

Why the contradiction is not repairable by invoking lead time: in G2-PHELO-01 the analogous facts are consistent precisely because the diagnosis clock moves (survival from diagnosis lengthens while deaths at a fixed twelve years are unchanged). Here the stem forecloses that escape by asserting that survival from diagnosis 'does not differ', i.e. that the diagnosis clock did NOT move in the attenders, even though the attenders were screened. With the clock origin fixed and incidence fixed, the claimed disease-specific mortality difference has no mechanism left to arise through.

Consequence for the teaching point: the confounding the item wants to demonstrate must act on some quantity, and the stem has stipulated every available quantity to be equal. Healthy-screenee confounding ordinarily produces lower disease mortality via lower incidence and/or lower case fatality (fitter, non-smoking, exercising people develop less disease and survive it better). The item has closed both channels in order to exclude overdiagnosis and lead-time bias, and in doing so has removed the mechanism by which its own key operates. Fix: delete or weaken clause (iii). Replacing 'survival measured from diagnosis does not differ between the groups' with a clause that closes lead-time on design grounds instead (for example, that the analysis compared mortality in the whole eligible cohort rather than survival after diagnosis, so the date of diagnosis plays no part in the comparison) excludes lead-time bias without asserting an impossible datum, and leaves the road-traffic-collision clause doing the real work.

Knock-on into the rationales (noted, not separately scored, since it merely restates the stem): distractor rationale A closes lead-time with 'Survival measured from diagnosis does not differ between these groups; what differs is mortality, including mortality from causes screening cannot touch.' That sentence inherits the impossible combination, so the exclusion of lead-time currently rests on a datum that could not be observed.

one_best_answer PASS despite the above: no other option survives. Only healthy screenee bias can explain 'lower mortality from causes the programme cannot affect, including road traffic collisions', which is the one finding no screening measurement artefact can produce. B remains uniquely defensible.

distractor_competitiveness PASS. Each distractor has a positive stem anchor and each is separately closed: A by 'survival measured from diagnosis does not differ' (subject to the defect above), C by 'the distribution of tumour grades and growth rates is the same', D by 'The cumulative number of people diagnosed with the disease is the same in both groups'. The mechanisms are described accurately in each rationale, and the exclusion of D ('That requires more cases in the screened group') correctly identifies excess cumulative incidence as the operational signature of overdiagnosis.

reasoning_demand PASS but only just. The chain 'Attendance was entirely voluntary and no one was allocated to a group' plus 'The attenders were less likely to smoke and more likely to exercise at baseline' plus lower non-disease mortality is a triple cue pointing at selection bias, and the key is reachable from the design cue alone for a candidate who never engages the three exclusion clauses. This is materially easier than G2-PHELO-01, where the single salient cue leaves three options alive. It clears the bar because the candidate must still recognise WHY mortality from road traffic collisions is diagnostic of pre-existing group difference, but the margin is thin.

material_redundancy PASS, with a substantive caveat. The two items DO test genuinely different decisions and discriminators: G2-PHELO-01 asks whether an unchanged mortality with a lengthened survival means the clock origin moved (measurement artefact inside a randomised comparison); G2-PHELO-05 asks whether an outcome advantage extending to causes screening cannot touch means the groups differed beforehand (confounding inside an observational comparison). Neither key is reachable by the other's reasoning, and each excludes the other's key on design grounds, so neither is subsumed. The redundancy that IS present is presentational and should be reduced: the lead-in is verbatim identical ('Which explanation best accounts for this pattern of results?'); the four options are the identical pool in a permuted order; the admitted evidence is the identical set of four claims; the exclusion clauses are near-verbatim ('the distribution of tumour grades and growth rates is the same', 'the cumulative number of people diagnosed ... is the same in both groups'); and the length-time and overdiagnosis distractor rationales are close paraphrases of each other across the two items. A candidate who meets both in one form learns the template rather than the epidemiology: find the clause that has NOT been neutralised. Recommend diverging the surface of one item (different lead-in, a different competitor in place of one shared option, and exclusion by study design rather than by a repeated identical clause) while keeping both, since the underlying decisions are distinct.
